title: VMU MQ-9 Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
2.     MOS 7318, VMU MQ-9 Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. MQ-9 Officers employ a network enabled and digitally
interoperable UAS, from a Ground Control Station, to provide RSTA, aviation
fires, and electromagnetic support across the full spectrum of combat
operations. MQ-9 Officers will advise supported commanders on matters
regarding UAS integration and provide information of intelligence value not
readily available from normal sources.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Security requirement: eligibility for top secret clearance with
sensitive compartmented information (TS/SCI).

        (3) Must meet the physical requirements per Manual of the Medical
Department, section IV, and article 15-100.

        (4) Must take the ASTB and score a four or higher on the AQR and a
six or higher on either the PFAR or the FOFAR.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the requirements for the BUQ-4 in accordance with CJCSI
3255.01 by any of the following methods:

                (a) Compete the USAF RPA Course:

                1. Pilot Flight Screening Course (C70RB1), at USAF Air
Education and Training Command, Pueblo, CO.



                                          1-271                       Enclosure (1)
 1142                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



                     2.   RIQ Course (F16RPA4) at USAF 558 FTS, Randolph AFB, TX.

                3.        RPA Fundamentals Course (RFC) (F16RPC4) at USAF 558 FTS,
Randolph AFB, TX.

            (b) Designated Naval Aviators have achieved the BUQ-4
requirements.

        (2) A BUQ-4 individual will be awarded the MOS 7318 after the
completion of the following course: MQ-9A Officer Initial Qualification
Training (IQT) Course (F34H331) at Holloman, AFB.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provides air support through UAS level 4 (function and control of
unmanned aircraft and payload minus takeoff and landing) and/or UAS level 5
(full function and control of unmanned aircraft and payload)
interoperability.

        (2) Performs EMSO against enemy communications, RADAR, and cyber
networks; plans and executes multi sensor imagery reconnaissance and
surveillance over assigned areas; advises, coordinates, and controls
supporting arms on behalf of the supported commander; and when directed,
destroys targets through kinetic or non-kinetic means.

        (3) Performs the duties as a member of the supported commander's
MAGTF information group (MIG).

            (4) Executes offensive and defensive tactics.

            (5) Supervises analysis, synthesis, and dissemination of information.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders/Managers, All Other
55-1019.

       f.   Related Military Skill.    None.

matches: Maintain air-to-ground and point-to-point radio contact with aircraft commanders.

MQ-9 Officers employ a network enabled and digitally interoperable UAS, from a Ground Control Station, to provide RSTA, aviation fires, and electromagnetic support across the full spectrum of combat operations.
Maintain air-to-ground and point-to-point radio contact with aircraft commanders.
MQ-9 Officers will advise supported commanders on matters regarding UAS integration and provide information of intelligence value not readily available from normal sources.
Use airfield landing and navigational aids and digital data terminal communications equipment to perform duties.

d. Duties (1) Provides air support through UAS level 4 (function and control of unmanned aircraft and payload minus takeoff and landing) and/or UAS level 5 (full function and control of unmanned aircraft and payload) interoperability.
Communicate fire details to superiors, subordinates, or interagency dispatch centers, using two-way radios.
(2) Performs EMSO against enemy communications, RADAR, and cyber networks.
Operate airborne remote sensing equipment, such as survey cameras, sensors, or scanners.
plans and executes multi sensor imagery reconnaissance and surveillance over assigned areas.
advises, coordinates, and controls supporting arms on behalf of the supported commander.
Develop defense plans or tactics, using intelligence and other information.
Analyze and interpret news and information received from various sources to broadcast the information.
(5) Supervises analysis, synthesis, and dissemination of information.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
